tb21_profile.skill: Build a legacy C program from a Debian/Ubuntu source package: fetch and extract the distro source, configure/patch the Makefile to disable an optional feature (X11 graphics), compile without the missing library, install the binary to /usr/local/bin, and confirm it is not linked against the excluded library.
tb21_profile.domain: C build toolchain (make, gcc, conditional compilation), Debian source packages (apt-get source / dpkg-source), Unix packaging and install prefixes; the pMARS Core War simulator.
tb21_profile.task_form: build/packaging from source with a feature-disable constraint and an install-and-verify step.

verifier_notes: No grade I relied on was wrong. Terminal-Lego's apt-source-config task_02572 is FREE and was left out. RTS build-from-source tasks are all 'absent' (no verifier shipped); they match the task_form well but graded CalibForge/TW equivalents exist, so RTS stays out of final_top10 per the spec's preference. CalibForge picks are graded ok/strong and their suites run the built binary (e.g. htop --version, cmatrix -h) and check linkage, matching the grade.

notes: CalibForge again wins, but this task is unusual in that Terminal-Lego and TerminalWorld are genuinely competitive on task_form. The two CalibForge twins are near-literal: software-engineering_20260420_020307_001 builds htop from Ubuntu source packages while disabling optional linkage (libcap/libsensors), extracts source to /app, installs to /usr/local/bin, and verifies the binary is not linked to the excluded libs - structurally identical to build-pmars-without-X11; and cmatrix (autotools, /usr/local/bin, verify linkage) is the same compile-small-C-program-and-install pattern. CalibForge takes 5 of the final 10, all its build-from-source cluster graded ok/strong. TerminalWorld is a real second here: it has a large, honest set of 'build/compile <C or C++ project> from source and install' tasks (GiNaC, libwebsockets, Singularity, suanPan, Denarius, LainOS cross-compile) that match task_form 5/5, unlike its usual FREE-heavy showing - 3 reach final. Terminal-Lego contributes the single best domain match for the source-acquisition step (task_00260 uses apt-get source to pull a C program's Debian source, exactly what pMARS asks) plus a cluster of 'satisfy the missing native build dependency then recompile' tasks (pcre.h, libcurl, JNI headers); 2 reach final. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has strong task_form (a big network-manager-l2tp autotools cluster: install deps, autogen.sh, ./configure with flags, compile; plus a PostgreSQL-from-tarball build) but ships NO verifier (all absent), so despite being some of the most literal build-from-source matches in the pool, they are held out of final in favour of graded equivalents - flag this to the merge step, because if absent candidates are acceptable, rts_task_a1fb5d219782b2ad9fd0ccbe (PostgreSQL from source) and the l2tp configure-with-flags tasks would rank around final positions 4-9. SWE-Smith (conan build-system/compiler-flag bugs) and SWE-Rebench (setuptools/conda/pip-tools build plumbing) transfer only weakly - right domain layer, wrong task_form (issue-fix, not build-from-source) - and neither reaches final. Downstream: this TB2.1 task is well covered; CalibForge alone yields four 4-5 finalists, and if the merge wants maximum task_form fidelity the RTS autotools cluster is the untapped reserve, gated only by its missing verifier.
